chapter.title: Character and speech
chapter.story: He travelled east to study and was laughed at for his accent until he outlasted everyone in the circle.

pages.saying: Whoever gives charity equal to a date from honest earnings, Allah accepts it and makes it grow, as you would raise a foal, until it becomes like a mountain.
pages.idris: A date. That's all. Started honestly, it grows.
pages.found: Ma'n found a page lining an old hat bought from a pedlar.

pages.saying: Protect yourselves from the Fire, even with half a date given in charity.
pages.idris: Half a date. There's no excuse left after that.
pages.found: Dawud hands you a loaf wrapped in an old page. “Look at the writing on this.”

pages.saying: When a person dies, his deeds end except three: ongoing charity, knowledge that benefits, and a righteous child who prays for him.
pages.idris: The fountain you mended will still be running when we're both gone.
pages.found: Usama found a folded page in a crack while mending a wall. “It's in a scholar's hand. You'll know who wants it.”

pages.saying: The Prophet sent Mu'adh to Yemen and told him zakat is taken from their rich and given back to their poor.
pages.idris: Zakat isn't a gift. It's the poor's share, held in your hand for a while.
pages.found: Children are flying a kite made from an old page. Ma'n buys it from them for a date and gives it to you.

pages.saying: No one hoards food to raise its price except a sinner.
pages.idris: Jalal's storehouses. Now you know why the qadi acted.
pages.found: Dawud found a page pressed inside a second-hand book.

pages.saying: Give the worker his wages before his sweat dries.
pages.idris: Sumayya's pickers. Late wages are a debt that grows heavier every night.
pages.found: Usama has been using a page to wrap spices and has only just noticed the writing.

pages.saying: A merchant used to tell his servants: if a debtor is struggling, let him off, so that Allah may let us off. And Allah forgave him.
pages.idris: Ma'n's flood. Karim's patience. This page is for both of them.
pages.found: Ma'n pulls a damp page from the bottom of a basket and dries it for you.

pages.saying: The Messenger of Allah cursed the one who gives a bribe and the one who takes it.
pages.idris: Both hands are dirty in a bribe. Wahb's and the one who fills it.
pages.found: Dawud found a page under a loose floor tile.

pages.saying: In wine, ten people are cursed - including the one who carries it and the one it is carried to.
pages.idris: Qasim's jars. The carrier is not innocent because the jars aren't his.
pages.found: Usama was given a debt note - and the scholar's page is written on the back of it.

pages.saying: Prizes in contests are only for racing camels and horses and for archery.
pages.idris: Contests for skill, yes. Gambling for luck, no.
pages.found: Ma'n's little one folded a page into a paper boat. Ma'n dried it out for you.
